statement: The top-8 edit installs a weak dose of RL's policy on every sample, but on a fixed subset of prompts the plain prompt still keys the plain base's own short, committed answer, so top8 plain's quick wrong answers are a per-problem plain-prompt failure: they fall on the problems that the unedited plain base itself gets wrong, not on random samples drawn at a flat ~50 % error rate whatever the problem.
why_strongest: It gives the same three measured values as the theory. Top8's quick wrong answers are short (0.77 at <= 1,000 tokens) because they are plain-base answers. They sit on problems the cued base usually solves (cued 4-sample rate 0.82; 0.25 of top8-wrong problems are cued 4/4) because plain-prompt failures depend on the prompt and register, not on how hard the problem is for the cued base. The other facts fit too: 22 quick wrong answers against the cued base's 13, top8 about 1.29x the cued base's length, and only 0.36 of the cued base's wrong problems shared. It also fits the board: the plain base is wrong on 276/500 and opens in the cue's register on its own only on some prompts (168/500 at T 0.6), WSP-2's prompt-keyed hand edit writes the cue on 96/100 rather than all of them, and a same-seed rerun changes few scores, so per-problem propensity dominates. The theory and this rival differ only in what decides which answers drop into the plain register: per-sample chance (theory) or the prompt (rival). Only rows from an independent plain-base sample can separate the two.

tests.experiment: Plain-base T 1.0 wrong rate on the problems where top8 plain gives a quick finished-wrong answer.
tests.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json and S3 s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (base, plain, T 1.0; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md). Selected set Q = top8 rows with score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false and n_generated <= 2000 (rows with missing score_v3 left out; each problem_index once, first row in file order). In T3 keep the first row per problem_index and compute its v3 score with studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold (empty extraction = 0). A T3 row is wrong if its v3 score is 0 or cap_hit is true. Drop problems in Q that have no T3 row. Statistic: (number of problems in Q whose T3 row is wrong) / (number of problems in Q with a T3 row).
tests.theory_should_say: If the plain-register failure is a per-sample coin flip that ignores the problem, an independent plain-base sample on these mostly cued-easy problems is wrong at about its usual rate on such problems, about 0.45-0.5. The rival says the same prompts trip the plain base, which gives about 0.7.

tests.experiment: Difficulty-controlled contrast: plain-base T 1.0 wrong rate on top8's quick-wrong problems minus its wrong rate on top8-right problems that the cued base solves in at least 3 of 4 samples.
tests.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json, studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, and S3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. T3: first row per problem_index, v3 recomputed with studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold; wrong = v3 score 0 or cap_hit true. Group Q = top8 rows with score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false, n_generated <= 2000 (missing score_v3 left out; first row per problem_index). Group C = top8 rows with score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit false whose problem has exactly 4 attempt-0 rows in rows.jsonl with at least 3 of them score_v3 == 1. Problems without a T3 row are dropped from both groups. Statistic: (fraction of Q with T3 wrong) - (fraction of C with T3 wrong).
tests.theory_should_say: Under per-sample switching, which problems fail is unrelated to the plain base's own failures beyond difficulty. Q is only slightly harder than C for the cued base, so the theory implies a small gap of about 0.0-0.1, against the rival's 0.25.

tests.experiment: Plain-base T 0.6 wrong rate (a second, independent plain sample) on the problems where top8 plain gives a quick finished-wrong answer.
tests.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json and S3 s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md). Q as in the first test (top8 score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false, n_generated <= 2000; missing score_v3 left out; first row per problem_index). In P_math500 keep, for each problem_index, the row with the smallest sample value; compute its v3 score with studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold (empty extraction = 0). Wrong = v3 score 0 or cap_hit true. Drop problems in Q without a P_math500 row. Statistic: (number of problems in Q whose P_math500 row is wrong) / (number of problems in Q with a row).
tests.theory_should_say: The plain base at T 0.6 is right on 319/500 overall and more often on cued-easy problems. If top8's quick failures are sample-level chance, this independent sample is wrong on about 0.3-0.35 of Q. The rival puts the failure in the prompt and expects about 0.55.
